newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Sihanouk says unhappy on throne but won't abdicate.
newsitem.headline: Sihanouk says unhappy on throne but won't abdicate.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk said in an interview published on Wednesday he was unhappy on the throne but vowed he would not abdicate to run in general elections next year.
Sihanouk, who left for Beijing for an eye operation and a medical checkup, said: "I have never found myself at ease as king."
The 74-year-old monarch said he had been "seriously thinking of abdicating" but had pledged not to step down before 2000 to reassure those who feared he would run in next year's elections.
"I will never stand in these legislative elections in 1998," Sihanouk said in the written interview conducted by his cabinet and released by the palace.

The king's trip to China comes at a time of heightened tensions between the Cambodian People's Party (CPP) and the royalist FUNCINPEC party, which formed an uneasy coalition government after U.N.-run elections in 1993.
The king's son, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, leads FUNCINPEC.
Some analysts believe the CPP and its leader, co-premier Hun Sen, fear the king might quit to lead a royalist party to victory at the polls on the back of his grassroots popularity.

Sihanouk denied in the interview he would start a new party or seek to revive the Sangkum Reastr Niyum (SRN), a mass political organisation he founded upon abdicating for the first time in 1955 to give him greater political freedom.
The constitution that restored Sihanouk to the throne in 1993 provides for a monarch who reigns but does not rule.
Sihanouk said there was a growing republican and anti-Sihanouk movement that had infiltrated the major parties and gained influential and important posts. He did not mention any names.
Newspapers regarded as supporters of the CPP or pro-republican have launched periodic attacks on the king and his wife.
A royal palace official said Sihanouk would undergo a regular medical check-up in Beijing and was likely to be away for a month.
The king has managed to beat cancer but suffers from a range of other ailments, including arterio-sclerosis and diabetes. He said he would have a cataract operation on his right eye while in Beijing.
